cases.prompt: improve the README for this project
cases.expected_output: An updated README.md that keeps whatever was already accurate, restructures it to follow the skill's section order (hero, badges, what-is-this, quick start, structure, docs table, contributing, optional connect, star history footer), and fills gaps using facts actually detected in the repo — not a rewrite that invents content the repo doesn't support.
assertions: README.md exists and was modified, not left untouched
Section order matches assets/readme-template.md (hero/badges first, contributing/social/star-history last)
No {{PLACEHOLDER}} tokens remain unresolved anywhere in the output
Install/run commands in Quick Start match the actual detected package manager and real scripts (e.g. from package.json), not a generic or guessed command
Any pre-existing accurate content (e.g. a correct project description) is preserved or improved, not deleted without reason
Badges present only correspond to things confirmed to exist (real license file, real CI workflow, real GitHub remote)

cases.prompt: my repo needs a better README, can you make it look professional? it's kind of a mess right now
cases.expected_output: A polished, professional-reading README that fixes structure/tone problems without adding marketing fluff or fabricated claims — casual phrasing in the request should not lower the bar on fact-grounding.
assertions: Tone matches the Writing Tone guidance in references/readme-best-practices.md: concrete and specific, no unverifiable superlatives like 'blazing-fast', 'next-generation', 'revolutionizes'
Hero section is centered with project name, one-line tagline, and a badge row, per assets/readme-template.md
Every badge and link resolves to a real, detected value (git remote owner/repo, real license, real CI workflow) — nothing fabricated to look more impressive
'Professional' is achieved through structure and clarity, not through invented sections that don't apply to this project (per Adapting to Project Type)
No leftover placeholder text (e.g. 'OWNER/REPO', 'TODO', lorem ipsum) in the final output

cases.prompt: Generate a README for this project. It's just a small script, nothing fancy.
cases.expected_output: A short README proportional to a small-utility project: a tight Quick Start and a clear usage example, without padding in unnecessary sections — following the Small utility / script row in the Adapting to Project Type table.
assertions: README is noticeably short — no 12-section README for a single-script project
Quick Start is present and is a single tight block with the real run command
Contributor avatar grid, star history chart, and social badges are omitted (not applicable to a small solo-maintainer script per Adapting to Project Type)
No project structure tree or docs table section if the project has no meaningful subdirectories or docs to link
No mermaid architecture diagram — skipped per the Mermaid Diagrams guidance for single-file utilities
Description is specific to what the script actually does, not generic filler expanded to fill space

cases.prompt: I want to add some nice badges to my README, the shields.io kind. Can you help?
cases.expected_output: A badge row added/updated in the README using exact shields.io URL formats from assets/badges.json, all with style=for-the-badge, limited to 3-5 status badges, and only for things that actually exist in the repo — no fabricated badges for nonexistent CI, releases, or social channels.
assertions: Every badge URL uses style=for-the-badge and matches a format defined in assets/badges.json
Badge {{PLACEHOLDER}} values (OWNER, REPO, WORKFLOW_FILE, PACKAGE, etc.) are all resolved to real detected values, never left as literal placeholder text
Status badge count is in the 3-5 sweet-spot range, not a long row of every possible badge
No CI badge added if no CI workflow file was found; no version badge if there are no releases/tags; no social badges for platforms with no detected link
Badges are placed in the hero section directly under the title/tagline, per README Structure in SKILL.md
If the repo doesn't actually have things to badge (e.g. no CI, no license file), the response says so rather than inventing a badge anyway
